¶ 53. trance] Written above storm canc. in Nbk 11.
 Cp. Misery. — A Fragment 3 (Longman iii, no. 202) 5: ‘While my burning heart lies sleeping’. The
untidily reworked draft appears to include the cancelled reading: ‘and die/A [?brand] consumed with
fires unseen’.
 And dream the rest] In Eloisa to Abelard, Eloisa urges the now-castrated Abelard to visit her so that she
may ‘to thy heart be pressed;/Give all thou canst — and let me dream the rest’ (123–4).
 Could] Couldst 1824. what] as 1824. The 1824 readings would appear to be Mary’s amendments
of the draft.
 It is very difficult to distinguish between cancellation and underlining for restoration or reconsider-
ation in the draft of this stanza, in a mixture of pencil and ink with much overwriting. The text given here
satisfies sense and prosody, and may represent S.’s final intention, though he might have revised it further had
